statement: Let (X_1, \dots, X_n) be independent, identically distributed real random variables with common cumulative distribution function F(t). The empirical distribution function \widehat{F}_n(t) is defined as \widehat{F}_n(t) = \frac{\text{number of elements in the sample} \le t}{n} = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathbf{1}_{X_i \le t}, where \mathbf{1}_A is the indicator of event A.

symbols.meaning: empirical cumulative distribution function evaluated at t
true common cumulative distribution function evaluated at t
indicator function of the event X_i <= t

properties.why: For fixed t, \mathbf{1}_{X_i \le t} is a Bernoulli random variable with parameter p = F(t), making n\widehat{F}_n(t) a binomial random variable with mean nF(t)
n\widehat{F}_n(t) is a binomial random variable with variance nF(t)(1 - F(t))
\widehat{F}_n(t) jumps up by 1/n at each of the n data points

properties.property: Pointwise almost sure convergence: \widehat{F}_n(t) \xrightarrow{\text{a.s.}} F(t) as n \to \infty
properties.why: Follows by the strong law of large numbers applied to the i.i.d. Bernoulli indicator variables

properties.property: Pointwise asymptotic normality: \sqrt{n}(\widehat{F}_n(t) - F(t)) \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{N}(0, F(t)(1 - F(t)))
properties.why: Follows from the central limit theorem applied to the sample mean of Bernoulli indicators
Has the same asymptotic properties because the ratio (n + 1)/n approaches 1 as n goes to infinity

assumptions.assumption: The sample observations X_1, \dots, X_n are independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.) draws from common CDF F(t).
assumptions.breaks_when: Observations are statistically dependent, non-identically distributed, or subject to distribution shift.

assumptions.assumption: The sample size n is a positive integer (n >= 1).
assumptions.breaks_when: The sample is empty (n = 0), causing division by zero in 1/n.

failure_modes.mode: High variance and coarse discretization at small sample sizes
failure_modes.signature: Large discrete jumps of magnitude 1/n and substantial pointwise deviations |\widehat{F}_n(t) - F(t)|.
failure_modes.cause: Variance scales as F(t)(1 - F(t))/n, which is large when n is small.

failure_modes.mode: Estimator inconsistency and bias under non-i.i.d. data
failure_modes.signature: \widehat{F}_n(t) fails to converge to F(t) almost surely or exhibits systematic estimation bias.
failure_modes.cause: Violation of the i.i.d. assumption invalidates the Bernoulli/binomial distribution structure and the strong law of large numbers.
